Laura / team — I reviewed BrightEdge's redlines and summarized the material points below:

1) Data transfers: they want express consent to route EU data under their SCC implementation. We can accept SCCs but need to confirm we can list subprocessors and provide a timely data transfer impact notice.
2) Subprocessors: they added a right to audit subprocessor list quarterly. We can offer quarterly updates and SOC2 evidence but not an on-site audit without an NDA and scoped review.
3) Liability cap: they asked to raise the cap for security breaches. We can offer a carveout for gross negligence.
4) Retention / deletion: they asked for immediate deletion on termination; propose 90 days for our operational retention to drain caches and backups.

If BrightEdge can accept the compromise on retention and on the auditor scope, we should be able to sign. We will provide SOC2 snippets and the current subprocessor roster as a separate zipped attachment upon request.

For execution: Laura — please confirm who will be the primary signer in our system. My recommendation for routing in DocuSign:
- Signer 1: BrightEdge (customer)

- Signer 3: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com (VP Legal) — set as a signing step that can be skipped if not required (if the contract value/term thresholds do not trigger countersign)

If you prefer we can accept a single countersign by Laura and use Rishi only for final countersign (manual) to speed up process.
